meal.title: Putting Student and Account classes together
meal.objective: Instantiate Student and Account objects and call their methods to see OOP in action

voice.script: What happens when you bring a student and a bank account together? In Python, a class is a blueprint for creating objects. An object, also called an instance, is a concrete copy of that blueprint that holds its own data. A method is a function defined inside a class that works on its instance. The print function displays text on the terminal. Now let's see the code. First we create two Student instances named Alice and Bob, add a few marks to each, and ask them to print their average. Then we create an Account instance for Alice, deposit money, withdraw some, and print the balance. Running the program shows the methods in action, confirming that each object keeps its own data and responds to commands.

visual.code:
class Student:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
        self.marks = []
    def add_mark(self, mark):
        self.marks.append(mark)
    def average(self):
        if not self.marks:
            print(f"{self.name} has no marks.")
            return
        avg = sum(self.marks) / len(self.marks)
        print(f"{self.name}'s average is {avg}")

class Account:
    def __init__(self, owner):
        self.owner = owner
        self.balance = 0
    def credit(self, amount):
        self.balance += amount
    def debit(self, amount):
        self.balance -= amount
    def get_balance(self):
        print(f"{self.owner}'s balance is {self.balance}")

alice = Student("Alice")
bob = Student("Bob")
alice.add_mark(85)
alice.add_mark(90)
bob.add_mark(70)
bob.add_mark(75)
alice.average()
bob.average()

alice_acc = Account("Alice")
alice_acc.credit(1000)
alice_acc.debit(250)
alice_acc.get_balance()
